idiom_name: Map<id, {resolve, reject}> around a Promise + timer deadline
implementation_notes: A Promise plus a Map of its resolver functions is the whole pattern: each call mints an id, stores resolve/reject under it, sends and returns the promise, and the message handler looks the id up, deletes the entry and settles the promise - no class structure is required, which is why the shape hides inside libraries such as websocket-as-promised and most JSON-RPC clients. Promise itself has no cancellation protocol, so the deadline is a timer that deletes the entry and rejects, or a race against a rejecting timeout promise. On the server side AsyncLocalStorage from node:async_hooks keeps the current correlation id available to logs and downstream calls without threading it through every function signature.
pitfalls: A promise whose entry is deleted without being settled hangs its caller forever (and in Node can keep the process alive) - every removal path must settle or knowingly abandon the caller.
Timers keep the event loop alive: clear them when the reply arrives and consider unref() for long deadlines inside libraries.
The Map grows without bound if a transport silently stops delivering, so the timeout delete is the only thing reclaiming entries - monitor its size in long-lived processes.
JSON keys are strings and integers above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER lose precision, so keep correlation ids as strings on the wire or an id echoed by another runtime will not match.
